facts.fact_text: On 6 May 2012 a public demonstration entitled the 'March of Millions' was held in central Moscow.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration on 6 May 2012 was held to protest against the allegedly rigged presidential elections.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration on 6 May 2012 had been approved by the Moscow city authorities in the form of a march followed by a meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
The first applicant (Mr Aristov) and the second applicant (Mr Gromov) took part in the demonstration on 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square.
According to the second applicant (Mr Gromov), on 6 May 2012 at 4 p.m. he came to Bolotnaya Square to participate in the authorised demonstration.
When the marchers arrived at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, it became apparent that barriers installed by the police had narrowed the entrance to the meeting venue.
The barriers installed by the police at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 allegedly restricted the space allocated for the meeting.
To control the crowd at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, a police cordon forced the protestors to remain within the barriers.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police ordered that the meeting at Bolotnaya Square finish early.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police began to disperse the participants of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square.
The first applicant (Mr Aristov) and the second applicant (Mr Gromov) were arrested at the venue of the demonstration on 6 May 2012.
After their arrest, the first applicant (Mr Aristov) and the second applicant (Mr Gromov) were brought to police stations where they were charged with administrative offences.
After an overnight detention, the first applicant (Mr Aristov) and the second applicant (Mr Gromov) were brought before the justices of the peace and convicted as charged.
According to the Government, the second applicant (Mr Gromov) was arrested at 8.10 p.m. on 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square.
At 9 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the second applicant (Mr Gromov) was brought to Veshnyaki district police station in Moscow.

At Veshnyaki district police station, an on-duty officer drew up a record of the second applicant's (Mr Gromov's) administrative escort at 9.10 p.m. on 6 May 2012 for the purpose of compiling an administrative-offence record.
At 9.20 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the second applicant (Mr Gromov) was administratively arrested at Veshnyaki district police station.
The first applicant (Mr Aristov) was accused of having disobeyed a lawful order of the police, an offence under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The second applicant (Mr Gromov) was accused of having disobeyed a lawful order of the police, an offence under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
According to the Government, the first applicant (Mr Aristov) was arrested because he had disregarded police orders to cease his actions at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
According to the Government, the second applicant (Mr Gromov) was arrested because he had disregarded the police order to cease breaking the police cordon and to disperse.
There were numerous clashes between the police and protesters at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
According to the first applicant (Mr Aristov), he did not cause any disorder at the time of his apprehension on 6 May 2012.
According to the first applicant (Mr Aristov), he did not resist the police officers who arrested him on 6 May 2012.
According to the Government, the first applicant (Mr Aristov) was arrested because he had participated in breaking the police cordon at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
The administrative-offence record against the first applicant (Mr Aristov) stated that during the event the participants broke the police cordon and tried to enter Red Square.

The administrative-offence record against the first applicant (Mr Aristov) stated that the applicant did not react to the multiple lawful demands of Officers P. and Ch. to stop breaking the police cordon and continued his unlawful acts, in breach of Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
According to the Government, the second applicant (Mr Gromov) was arrested because he was participating in breaking the police cordon at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.

The administrative-offence record against the second applicant (Mr Gromov) contained a printed template stating that the police repeatedly announced through a loudhailer lawful demands to stop the march but the applicant, acting as part of a group of citizens, broke the police cordon.

The administrative-offence record against the second applicant (Mr Gromov) stated that the applicant did not react to multiple demands to cease these actions and disperse, and continued his unlawful acts, thereby attracting the attention of the public and mass media.

The administrative-offence record against the second applicant (Mr Gromov) stated that the applicant tried to cause confusion among the public (создать суматоху среди граждан), thereby demonstrating his refusal to obey the lawful orders of the police officers and precluding them from fulfilling their service duties, in breach of Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
